name: EU machinery manual deadlines
buyer: US machine builders shipping into Europe, and the people who translate their manuals
cadence_long: One dated reading of one regulation
short: The dates and article numbers behind Europe's new machinery manual rules
who: US machine builders shipping into Europe, and the people who translate their manuals.
note: BORN NOT FOR SALE 2026-08-25. WHAT THE PAGE IS: one dated reading of one published European regulation, turned into the thing a US machine builder actually needs -- the deadlines, the article number behind each one, the 31 countries and the languages a manual has to be in. The reading date is 2026-08-24 and it comes from the saved rules file's own written_on, never from this machine's clock. DATES AND ARTICLE NUMBERS ONLY, NO EU TEXT, AND IT IS ENFORCED NOT PROMISED. There is no written permission record for the regulation's publisher anywhere on this box, so the page carries none of their words. check_no_eu_text() in the slice script reads the FINISHED page back and refuses to write it if any guarded sentence of the regulation is on it, after flattening accents, curly quotes, dashes, spacing and tags so a retyped sentence cannot slip past; family_spec() runs the same guard over every string it is about to return. It caught a real leak on its first run: declaration box 4 is a verbatim EU sentence, so that box is printed WITH ITS WORDING HELD BACK, named and counted on the page in plain words rather than quietly dropped -- the page says so out loud, because a page that silently omits what a reader came for is worse than one that says why. sample_status IS 'on-page' AND THAT IS THE HONEST WORD: there is no file behind this page and there never will be, so there is nothing to sample. It is not 'fail' -- fail means a file exists and is wrong. The required sentence is IMPORTED from scripts/slice_free_time.py rather than typed a third time, and the pill is drawn by the renderer off the catalog status, never printed by this module. NO NUMBER, DATE, PRICE, GROUP, CADENCE OR BUYER IS TYPED INTO THE PAGE. The module reads group, cadence, cadence_long, buyer and price out of THIS row with no fallback, and every count off the lane at build time. Counted off the shipped bytes: 6 deadlines (4 calendar dates -- 2027-01-20 three times under Articles 54, 51(2) and 52(1), and 2026-10-20 under Article 50(2) -- plus 2 lengths of time), 14 items read out of the regulation of which 12 are verified, 1 withdrawn and 1 unverified and the page says which, 31 countries, 14 languages that can be fact-checked, 11 declaration boxes with 1 wording withheld, 20 regulation sentences held off the page, 3 invented manuals. THE LANE'S STORE IS EMPTY AND THE PAGE SAYS SO: 0 manuals, 0 checks. Nobody has submitted one because there is nowhere to submit one and nothing is for sale. There is no upload service, no form and no account -- this estate's platform is not ours to add one to. ONE STAMP ON THE PAGE IS THE BUILD DATE AND THAT IS CORRECT: the section headed 'We ran our checker over 3 invented manuals' is stamped with the day the checker actually ran, because runs() imports the lane's real checker and calls it during the build. That stamp is the evidence for that section and it moves on every rebuild. Do not pin it to a fixed date -- that would make it a claim with nothing behind it. SAFE TO MERGE INTO catalog.json: unlike a feed-shaped family, this one does not trip scripts/check_built.py when the row moves out of this fragment. check_built skips an 'on-page' family because there is no store holding a newer row for a freshness tag to name -- the day it was read is on the page in words instead. Proved with the row merged: check_built raw exit 0.
